summary:
With many range-sum questions on the same data, precompute prefix sums once: `prefix[k]` = total of the
first k days. Then the total from day l to day r is `prefix[r + 1] − prefix[l]`, one subtraction per query.
O(n + q) instead of O(n · q).

question.md:
For each query `[l, r]`, return `sales[l] + … + sales[r]` (both ends included), in query order.

- **Many queries on unchanged data:** up to 10⁵ queries over up to 10⁵ days. Summing each range directly
  could take 10¹⁰ steps.
- **Big numbers:** values reach ±10⁹ and a range can contain 10⁵ of them, so totals reach ±10¹⁴. Use
  64-bit integers for the prefix sums (`[10⁹, 10⁹]` already sums past the 32-bit limit).
- **Single-day queries** like `[3, 3]` are allowed.

think.md:
Take `sales = [3, -1, 4, 1, 5, 9, -2]`. The total of days 1 … 4 is −1 + 4 + 1 + 5 = 9.

Think of the running total `prefix`: `prefix[k]` is the sum of the first k days. The first 5 days sum to
`prefix[5] = 12`, and the first 1 day to `prefix[1] = 3`. Days 1 … 4 are "the first 5 days
minus the first 1 day": 12 − 3 = 9.

The extra slot `prefix[0] = 0` (the sum of no days) is what makes ranges starting at day 0 work without a
special case.

approaches.title: Add up each range

idea.md: For each query, loop from l to r adding sales (64-bit).

build: For each query: `total = 0`; add `sales[k]` for k in l … r.

lines.text: Each query walks its whole range, adding in 64 bits.

complexity.md: **Time O(n · q)** in the worst case (every query spans everything). **Space O(1)** besides the output.

walk.title: Answer every query by adding up its range directly.

limits.md: Overlapping ranges are added again and again. Precomputing running totals lets every query reuse the same work.

idea.md: `prefix[0] = 0`, `prefix[k + 1] = prefix[k] + sales[k]` (64-bit). Each query `[l, r]` is `prefix[r + 1] − prefix[l]`.

lines.text: Running totals, one longer than the input so `prefix[0]` is the empty sum. 64-bit, because totals reach 10¹⁴.
Days l … r = (first r + 1 days) − (first l days).

notes.c: Free the prefix array; the caller frees `out`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n + q):** one pass to build, O(1) per query. **Space O(n)** for the prefix sums.

steps.text: prefix[k] = total of the first k days; prefix[0] = 0.

walk.title: Build prefix sums once; each query is then one subtraction.

takeaways.md:
- **Many range-sum queries on static data → prefix sums.** `sum(l … r) = prefix[r + 1] − prefix[l]`.
- Give the prefix array a leading 0 to avoid special-casing ranges that start at 0.
- Watch the width: sums of many 32-bit values need 64 bits.
